Subject: Coverage plan: extended caregiving leave (case HR-2026-0931)

Hi team,

Per our 1:1 today, Priya (not cc'd) has submitted a request for an extended caregiving leave starting 2026-03-15 for an estimated 12 weeks. Monica — thanks for flagging the case in HR. Im looping Rachel because shes our talent ops lead and will help coordinate short-term coverage and any backfill.

Attached: FMLA_request_20260215.pdf and a quick skill matrix I'm using to think about rotations (team_skill_matrix.xlsx).

High-level asks from my side:
- Short-term rotation plan to keep the Priority Search pipeline covered (we can reassign 2x weekly triage).
- Identify critical on-call windows and a primary backup owner.
- Recommend whether we hire a 12-week contractor or redistribute among ICs; include rough budget estimate.

I'll propose a 30-minute kickoff tomorrow at 11am to walk the plan. If Monica needs anything from benefits/vendor side, please advise.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Engineering Manager, Search
Redwood Inference

Attachments: FMLA_request_20260215.pdf (application form), team_skill_matrix.xlsx (stub)

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Coverage plan: extended caregiving leave (case HR-2026-0931)

Thanks, Lauren — I reviewed the FMLA packet. I put together a rotation-proposal-v1.xlsx with a suggested week-by-week assignment and a short list of tasks that must stay staffed (Search indexing, daily triage, customer escalations).

Key notes up front:
- Prefer redistribution for weeks 1-4, with a decision point at week 4 to either extend internal rotation or bring on a contractor for weeks 5-12.
- Cost estimate for a mid-level contractor (~$95/hr) for 8 weeks: ~$30k (rough).
- Need clear on-call owner for PagerDuty shifts weeks 3-12; recommend rotating pair for those weeks to avoid burnout.

I've attached the rotation proposal (rotation-proposal-v1.xlsx). I'll join the kickoff tomorrow.

Rachel Kim
Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rotation-proposal-v1.xlsx (stub)

Hi Lauren / Rachel,

Thanks for the quick coordination and for the attachments. A couple of compliance and benefits items before we finalize the operational plan:

1) Documentation: please confirm we have the medical certification/doctor_note_20260217.jpg on file. If not, Priya needs to submit it so we can confirm FMLA eligibility.
2) Benefits vendor workflow: Ive cc'd InsureServ (benefits@insureserv.com) so they can begin the formal intake. They will provide confirmation and any short-term disability steps.
3) PTO and accruals: HR will calculate payout vs. hold for the leave period and share a breakdown.
4) Return-to-work plan: please include a proposed ramp timeline in the rotation spreadsheet (e.g., 2 weeks 60% followed by 2 weeks 80%). We typically capture that in the HR case file at hr.redwood.ai.

Operationally, once InsureServ verifies the documentation, we can approve redistribution for weeks 1-4 immediately. If a contractor hire is needed, that will require a manager approval and a short procurement note.

Im available for the kickoff and will bring the HR checklist.

Best,
